To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) We propose the middle ground between expert programmers and STM, namely, MOD, that allows less expert programmers to use durable datastructures that are easy to reason about, easy to use, and perform well.
1) We present a new library for persistent memory, called MOD, that allows programmers to build applications with multiple durable data structures.
MOD improves performance by 40%, speeds up applications by 38% and is relatively easy to use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new class of datastructures that are both recoverable and performant.
the question: How can we make durable programming easy? We believe that our answer, the library of MOD datastructures, is a step in that direction.
the problem of how to make PM practical for programmers and developers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MOD is a novel and promising approach for building persistent applications.
we have designed, implemented, and evaluated a library of persistent datastructures called MOD.
MOD provides a simple, easy to use, high performance, and recoverable library of persistent datastructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MOD provides a simple, easy to use, and efficient way to make datastructures recoverable in PM.
MOD is a new approach to building durable datastructures that is easy to use, performs well on PM and can be composed into more complex durable datastructures.
we have developed MOD, a new class of persistent datastructures that are easy to use, perform better than STM, and are recoverable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the middle ground of MOD can be a good choice for applications needing durable datastructures that are easy to use and that perform well.
